title: Residency-aware audit escrow exporter with WORM notarization and automated evidence pipeline
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build an automated audit-export pipeline that produces residency-aware evidence bundles for admin actions, config changes, and privileged access events. Each bundle must be write-once (WORM) attested, include cryptographic checksums and HSM timestamping hooks, and be deliverable to region-bound escrow locations. Scope: exporter service, manifest schema, notarization integration, scheduling and retention metadata, rollback/canary plan, and visibility in Console. Excludes: long-term archive storage UI (handled by separate archival job), and non-admin telemetry events.
acceptance_criteria: Exported evidence bundles contain canonicalized admin events, metadata (tenant, region, retention policy), and SHA-256 manifest
Each bundle is sealed to WORM storage with an HSM-signed timestamp or equivalent notarization and a verifiable receipt
Exporter respects per-tenant data residency rules and writes only to allowed region endpoints
Automated delivery to escrow endpoints or S3-compatible WORM buckets succeeds with retries and dead-lettering after N attempts
Console shows export job status, last successful export time, and per-tenant pending deliveries
Integration tests simulate failover and verify fallback to alternate region per routing policy without leaking data outside residency boundaries
Security review completed and acceptance attestation present in PR description
notes: PoC HSM stamping integration: runtime/hsm-stamp-poc branch (internal), results in PR #3245
Trade-offs: synchronous notarization increases export latency but provides stronger non-repudiation; opting for async notarization with final attestations to meet throughput targets
Retention model: bundles are labelled with retention policy and TTL metadata; exporter sets lifecycle tags for downstream retention enforcer
Legal requested inclusion of human-readable manifest summarizing event counts, top-level hash, and canonicalization algorithm metadata

implementation_plan: Phase 1: exporter service + manifest schema + regional write adapters (2 sprints). Phase 2: HSM/KMS notarization integration and attestation receipts (1 sprint). Phase 3: Console integration and release gating + security review (1 sprint). Rollout: pilot with 3 non-production tenants, then opt-in GA for tenants with residency requirements.
risks: Notarization latency may cause downstream job queueing under peak load
Escrow endpoint misconfiguration could lead to failed deliveries and missed retention guarantees
Key compromise risk mitigated by HSM isolation and rotation policies but requires ops playbook
qa_plan: Unit tests for canonicalization and manifest generation
Integration tests: regional delivery + DLQ + resume semantics
Chaos test: simulate region unavailability and validate fallback does not violate residency constraints
Compliance e2e: verify WORM attestations and verifyability toolchain against sample bundles
